## Global Instructions

## Contributing

This applies to both humans and agents.

Each top-level directory is its own project unless it opts into shared
tooling. Use that project’s README, scripts, and conventions. Do not add a
root workspace, formatter, or check pipeline, or impose another project’s
stack.

### Code

- One approach per problem. Refactor duplication instead of leaving parallel
  implementations or defaults.
- Propagate failures (throw/exit). Do not swallow errors.
- Prefer a small function with a long name over a comment that restates the
  code. Reserve comments for non-obvious details (formats, limits, platform
  quirks).

### Commits

Use [13 Short Gitmojis](https://mmap.page/dive-into/gitmoji/). Write the
emoji **code** (e.g. `:bug:`), not the glyph.

```
:<type>:[scope:] <summary>
```

Scope is optional; prefer the project directory (`:new:foo: add CLI`).
Imperative summary; first line under 50 characters when practical. Add a
body when the motive is not obvious from the diff. Trailers last.

| code | usage |
|------|--------|
| `:bug:` | bug fix |
| `:new:` | new feature |
| `:fire:` | remove a feature / API surface (not merely deleting files) |
| `:boom:` | breaking changes |
| `:lock:` | security fix |
| `:art:` | refactor |
| `:zap:` | performance |
| `:100:` | test |
| `:memo:` | doc |
| `:zzz:` | chore |
| `:tada:` | release |
| `:poop:` | dirty hack / workaround |
| `:egg:` | Easter eggs |

Do not invent other gitmoji codes.

When they apply, trailers in this order:

1. `Reported-by: Name <email>` — someone else reported a bug this commit
   fixes
2. `Suggested-by: Name <email>` — someone else suggested the idea or
   approach
3. `Assisted-by: AGENT_NAME:MODEL_VERSION` — an AI agent produced or
   materially edited the tree

Do not credit agents with `Co-authored-by`. Do not force-push `master`.

Agent-only rules in the rest of these instructions add constraints; they do
not replace this section.

## Style

- Short, direct, technical prose
- On feedback/analysis: say agree or disagree, then what changed

## Code quality

- Read files in full before broad edits, audits, or changing unread files; do not rely on search snippets
- Ask before removing intentional behavior
- No shims unless asked

## Monorepos

When working in a monorepo:

- Prefer project-local configuration and follow project-local `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills/`
- Never edit or delete the root `README.md`

## Commands

- After creating/modifying a test: run it until it passes. No sleeps in tests.

## Skills

Always-on rules are an [APM](https://microsoft.github.io/apm/) package (`apm.yml`): source `.apm/instructions/*.instructions.md`. After editing them, run `apm install`, then `apm compile --target cursor --local-only --no-links --no-constitution` to regenerate Cursor rules and `AGENTS.md`. Cursor hooks are native (`.cursor/hooks.json`, `.cursor/hooks/`); APM does not manage them. In a monorepo, also follow project-local `AGENTS.md` and `.agents/skills/` when present.

User-level skills live in `skills/<name>/SKILL.md`. They are not APM primitives. Install by copying each directory to `~/.agents/skills/<name>/` (Cursor and Grok Build both load that path). When a task matches a skill description, read and follow that `SKILL.md`. **Before any commit**, read `skills/git-commits/SKILL.md` even if the user did not mention commits. After editing a skill, copy it to `~/.agents/skills/` again.

| Skill | Path |
|-------|------|
| Git commits and trailers | `skills/git-commits/SKILL.md` |
| Review one commit; fix after selection | `skills/review/SKILL.md` |
| Herdr (only when the user asks) | `skills/herdr/SKILL.md` |

## Herdr

Herdr is a terminal multiplexer for coding agents (workspaces, tabs, panes). Use it **only** when the user mentions Herdr or asks to inspect/control panes, tabs, workspaces, commands, or another agent — not merely because work could run in a background pane. Requires `HERDR_ENV=1`; if unset or not `1`, say you are not inside Herdr and stop. When using it, read and follow `skills/herdr/SKILL.md`.

## Git (multi-agent cwd)

Other agents may be editing different files here. Never touch their unstaged/staged/untracked files.

- Stage/commit only files **you** changed in **this** session; verify with `git status` first
- If you added, edited, or deleted any non-gitignored file this session, **commit before finishing your turn** — read the git-commits skill, stage your files, and commit. Never ask the user whether to commit
- Never push, force-push, or push/merge to `master` (even if asked)
- Never: `git reset --hard`, `git checkout .`, `git clean -fd`, `git stash`, `git add -A`, `git add .`, `git commit --no-verify`
- Rebase conflicts: resolve only your files; otherwise abort and ask
- Issues/PRs: only when explicitly asked; PRs must be drafts
